headline: Specialized Licensed Tour Access Required for Tundra Entry
reservation: Independent travel within Wapusk is not permitted for most visitors due to polar bear safety; access is typically via licensed commercial operators. You must distinguish between the park's remote research facilities and the guided excursions departing from Churchill. Changing permit requirements for research or photography groups necessitate a direct check with the Parks Canada Churchill office well in advance.

days.title: Coastal Tundra and Polar Bear Habitat

stops.name: Cape Churchill
stops.detail: Visit the world-renowned staging area for polar bears awaiting the freezing of the Hudson Bay.

stops.name: Hudson Bay Lowlands
stops.detail: Observe the unique permafrost landforms and peatlands that define this subarctic ecosystem.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours via Tundra Buggy; conditions vary by ice.
days.note: Access is restricted to specialized vehicles managed by licensed operators.

days.title: Subarctic Forest and Research History

stops.name: Nester One
stops.detail: See the primary research camp used for monitoring the park's biodiversity and climate change impacts.

stops.name: Owl River
stops.detail: View the transition zone where the northern boreal forest meets the open tundra.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours for helicopter or specialized transport; conditions vary.
days.note: Helicopter access is weather-dependent and requires advanced booking.

days.title: Churchill River Heritage

stops.name: Prince of Wales Fort
stops.detail: Explore the massive stone fortress nearby to understand the fur trade history that shaped the region.

stops.name: Sloop Cove
stops.detail: View historic inscriptions left by 18th-century explorers on the rocky shores.

days.driving: Allow 30-60 minutes for boat transfer; conditions vary.
days.note: Ensure your guide is equipped with bear deterrents for all shore excursions.

intel.title: Guided Access Only
intel.text: For safety, visitors must be accompanied by licensed guides or stay in fenced camps. Unauthorized entry into the park's interior is strictly prohibited.

intel.title: Bear Season Peaks
intel.text: Late October and November offer the best bear viewing, while February focuses on maternity denning. Plan travel months in advance as Churchill lodging fills quickly.

intel.title: Churchill Hub
intel.text: All fuel and food must be secured in Churchill; there are no services within Wapusk. Prices in town reflect the remote fly-in or rail-only nature of the community.

intel.title: Town-Only Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular signal is limited to the Churchill townsite and does not extend into the park. Guides utilize radio and satellite systems for communication.

intel.title: Train and Plane Staging
intel.text: There are no roads to Churchill; visitors arrive by rail or air. Local parking is generally limited to resident needs and small rental fleets.

plan.arrival: Arrival at Churchill Airport (YYQ) or Via Rail station, followed by an operator-led briefing and equipment check.
plan.vehicle: No private cars or RVs; transportation is limited to Tundra Buggies, helicopters, or specialized local watercraft.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset over the Hudson Bay from the Churchill coastline (seasonal variation).
